title: GeoTargetly body-hide is still live in production: three inline scripts each inject body{opacity:0} and gate first paint behind a remote JS callback, on every page

evidence.claim: Production HTML on 8 Aug contains 3 inline scripts, each inserting <style>body{opacity:0.0 !important;}</style> synchronously into head, un-hidden only when g10498469755.co/gr answers and the georedirect*loaded callback runs via setTimeout
evidence.source: curl https://www.cloudemployee.io/ (8 Aug); code at site/src/components/third-party-scripts.tsx (GEOTARGETLY_RULES, geoTargetlySnippet)
evidence.value: 6 occurrences of body{opacity:0.0 !important;} (3 rules x inline + RSC payload); rule IDs -OJz6mUkL51tX4CyQPmd, -OK8LE2WwpalZvadeMTu, -OK8QFN5yqnrUvZ_ZFAC

evidence.claim: If a redirect fires, the un-hide waits a further 5,000ms; verbatim in production HTML
Ahrefs Lighthouse LCP is Poor on 100% of 688 pages while server TTFB is under 200ms on 526 of 688 and load time under 500ms on 677 of 688; the page arrives and refuses to draw
evidence.source: Ahrefs dashboard aggregate read 8 Aug (no per-URL export on disk); server columns per-URL in ahrefs/site-audit/cloudemployee_06-aug-2026_internal-html-200-u_2026-08-08_09-40-13.csv
evidence.value: LCP 100% Poor; TBT ~40% Poor; CLS 100% Good; loadtime median 178ms

evidence.claim: Controlled Lighthouse runs (4 Aug): blocking GeoTargetly alone or HubSpot alone changes render delay by ~nothing; blocking both drops it from 5,007ms to 1,496ms, because the un-hide setTimeout is starved by HubSpot main-thread work
evidence.value: baseline perf 51 / render delay 5,007ms; both blocked perf 66 / 1,496ms

impact.estimate: Removes the mechanism that makes LCP Poor on 100% of 688 lab-measured pages. Measured floor: render delay 5,007ms to 1,496ms when both gates removed (SEO_PROGRAMME 2.1). Not a Google ranking input today (0 CrUX pages), but the first CrUX 28-day window is accumulating from launch traffic now, and this decides what it says.

recommendation: Move geo routing server-side and delete the body-hide. PERF-02 shows the country is already known server-side for free. Interim smaller step if the dashboard rules must stay: replace the JS-callback un-hide with a CSS animation timeout that cannot be starved by the main thread. Coordinate with CE-48 (GEO_ROUTING.md) which already specifies the target rule set.

title: The blocking geo round trip is redundant: the visitor country is already rendered into the HTML server-side from x-vercel-ip-country

evidence.claim: Production HTML carries window.VISITOR_COUNTRY set at HTML-generation time from Vercel's x-vercel-ip-country header, before any client JS runs
The three GeoTargetly snippets each make a blocking client round trip to g10498469755.co to determine the same fact
evidence.value: 6 references to g10498469755.co in homepage HTML

evidence.claim: GEO_ROUTING.md already argues the dashboard rules should move to the edge using this header
evidence.value: 'We already have the data for free'

impact.estimate: Enables PERF-01 to be a deletion rather than a mitigation: server-side redirect means zero flash, zero JS dependency, and removes a third-party host (g10498469755.co, 6 references) from in front of first paint on all 688 pages. Requires the CE-48 country list decision from Jake/Seb, so not a quick win by definition.

recommendation: Implement CE-48 in Next middleware or the layout using x-vercel-ip-country (the allow-list is already specified in GEO_ROUTING.md section 2), then remove all three GeoTargetly snippets and the body-hide with them. Heed Tech Debt #63: verify the PH team can still reach what they need before enabling any country redirect.

title: Every HTML response is served no-store with x-vercel-cache MISS: no CDN caching anywhere, and field TTFB is 1.37s desktop

evidence.claim: Live headers on /, /pricing, /our-work, /blog, /about-us all return cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0 and x-vercel-cache: MISS
evidence.value: no-store + MISS on 5 of 5 routes tested

evidence.claim: Vercel Speed Insights field TTFB is 1.37s desktop; live curl measured 0.95-1.82s on /; Ahrefs' crawler measured median 178ms from its infrastructure
evidence.source: Vercel Speed Insights 6-7 Aug; curl 8 Aug; ahrefs/site-audit/...internal-html-200-u...csv Loading time column

evidence.claim: Root layout calls headers() (VisitorCountryScript reads x-vercel-ip-country), which opts every route out of static rendering; sanityFetch/defineLive is the other dynamic dependency
evidence.value: await headers() in a component mounted in the root layout

impact.estimate: TTFB is the floor under every other metric: LCP cannot beat TTFB. Field desktop TTFB 1.37s already consumes 55% of the 2.5s Good LCP budget before a byte of content renders. Caching or ISR would take repeat TTFB toward the sub-200ms the Ahrefs crawler sees. Estimate: this plus PERF-01 is what moves LCP from Poor to Good; PERF-01 alone leaves LCP at ~4.2s (SEO_PROGRAMME 2.1 both-blocked run).

recommendation: After the geo work: isolate the headers() read (PPR, or move country injection to middleware/client) and give Sanity-backed routes ISR or cache tags so HTML can be CDN-cached. This is architectural and needs its own brief; do not attempt as a drive-by.

title: The per-route field spread (100 vs 46 desktop) is template payloads, not the server: sitewide cost and per-template cost are separable

evidence.claim: Ahrefs server-side metrics are uniform across templates: every template family has median fetch 131-394ms and median compressed size 18-47KB; no template is server-slow
evidence.source: ahrefs/site-audit/...internal-html-200-u...csv, 688 rows grouped by path template (analysis 8 Aug)
evidence.value: technology-detail n=192 med 164ms; blog-detail n=142 med 180ms; home med 302ms

evidence.claim: Vercel field desktop scores diverge widely by route on the same chrome: /pricing 100, /about-us 100, /services/software-engineers 100 vs /our-work 46, /blog detail 56, /contact 56, /services/fractional-ctos 55, / 81
evidence.value: spread of 54 points on identical sitewide chrome

evidence.claim: The poor routes carry identifiable heavy client payloads: homepage has a Vimeo background autoplay hero (player.vimeo.com/video/1131836141?background=1&autoplay=1), contact and book-a-call embed HubSpot forms/Calendly, blog details carry recovered video/table embeds
evidence.value: vimeo player referenced 3x in homepage HTML

impact.estimate: Per-template work is what separates a 100 route from a 46 route once sitewide gates are gone. Blog detail alone carries 222,042 of 488,153 GSC impressions in 90d (45.5%, joined/pages.json), so the worst-scoring template carries the largest search surface. See PERF-06 for the blog quantification.

recommendation: Fix sitewide first (PERF-01/02), re-measure, then do a facade pass per poor route: poster-image facade for the Vimeo hero, lazy-mount HubSpot forms and Calendly on interaction or viewport, audit /our-work (worst at 46) specifically. Do not start template work before the sitewide gates are removed or the measurements will be noise.

title: Lab and field do not contradict each other: the body-hide converts any main-thread slowness into blank screen, so throttled mobile lab collapses while fast desktop field often paints fine

evidence.claim: Ahrefs simulated-mobile Lighthouse: 0 of 588 Good, LCP 100% Poor. Vercel real-user desktop: several routes at 99-100
evidence.source: Ahrefs dashboard aggregate 8 Aug; Vercel Speed Insights 6-7 Aug

evidence.claim: The mechanism reconciles them: un-hide is a setTimeout gated on a ~165-227ms remote answer plus a free main thread. On fast desktop that resolves quickly; under mobile CPU throttle HubSpot's 3.6s main-thread work starves it for seconds
evidence.value: GeoTargetly endpoint answers 165-227ms; HubSpot 3,610ms main-thread blocking

evidence.claim: Vercel mobile field data is incoherent and must not be used as counter-evidence
evidence.value: 98 data points; FCP 5.36s > LCP 2.02s, impossible in one load

impact.estimate: Interpretive finding, no work item. Consequence: mobile users, who we currently cannot measure, are the population most likely to experience multi-second blank screens. Google's CrUX, when it arrives, is mobile-weighted.

recommendation: Treat lab mobile as the risk model for the unmeasured mobile population. Re-check Vercel mobile once sample size grows (later in Aug) and expect it to sit between lab mobile and field desktop.

title: Blog detail is the highest-stakes template: 45.5% of all GSC impressions (222k in 90d) on the template scoring 56 in field desktop

evidence.claim: Blog-detail pages carry 222,042 of 488,153 impressions in the 90d window across 65 pages with any impressions; clicks 126 of 1,235
evidence.source: joined/pages.json, impressions_90d/clicks_90d aggregated by template (talent excluded by construction)

evidence.claim: Blog detail scores 56 in Vercel field desktop, among the worst routes, and worst on both devices per the brief
Blog-detail server delivery is not the problem: 142 blog-detail rows have median fetch 180ms, median compressed size 34.7KB
Clicks are overwhelmingly brand-homepage: home takes 750 of 1,235 clicks (60.7%); blog impressions convert at ~0.06% CTR, consistent with mid-page-2 average positions

impact.estimate: Grounded ceiling, stated as an estimate: 222k impressions/90d is ~74k/month. Performance alone will not move mid-page-2 rankings to page 1, but blog detail is where any ranking-signal improvement is levered 45x harder than the average page. If average CTR merely doubled from 0.06% to 0.12% via better positions, that is ~44 extra clicks/month; a page-1 move on even a tenth of the impression base would be hundreds.

recommendation: After sitewide fixes, make blog detail the first template pass: lazy-mount recovered video/table embeds below the fold, verify the hero image request size, and re-measure this one template in the field before touching others.

title: 33 Sanity images total 59.7MB because transforms request w=3840 PNGs and multi-MB HEIFs with no format negotiation

evidence.claim: 33 image instances flagged too large, summing 59.73MB, every one a cdn.sanity.io URL

Pattern: PNGs requested at ?w=3840 without auto=format (4.0MB for a 1411x1001 source upscaled), and .heif sources that stay multi-MB even at ?w=384, implying the transform or format conversion is not applying
One 3.19MB image is inlinked from 10 pages, so a single asset fix propagates
evidence.source: same CSV, No. of IMG inlinks column

impact.estimate: Not the LCP cause (Ahrefs shows LCP Poor even on pages with no large image, and HTML transfer is 18-47KB), but 59.7MB of avoidable image weight across 33 instances, one hitting 10 pages. Mostly a mobile bandwidth and per-template LCP contributor on the specific pages that render them.

recommendation: Audit site/src/components/ui/image to ensure every Sanity URL carries auto=format plus a width matched to the rendered slot (not a blanket w=3840), and that HEIF sources are converted. Diagnosis-only note per repo debugging rules: confirm in a diagnosis pass, fix in an execution session.

title: Ahrefs 'all pages under 100KB' measures compressed transfer, not parse cost: the homepage is actually 525KB of HTML to parse

evidence.claim: curl without compression returns 525,489 bytes for /; with --compressed, 64,002 bytes. Ahrefs Size (bytes) for the same corpus is min 18,408 / median 33,257 / max 49,660, all under 100KB, matching the compressed number
evidence.value: 525KB raw vs 64KB gzip vs 33KB Ahrefs median (brotli)

evidence.claim: /our-work raw HTML is 321,952 bytes

impact.estimate: Mostly a measurement correction so nobody rules out page weight from the Ahrefs column. 525KB of HTML (largely the RSC flight payload duplicating page content) is a real parse cost on throttled mobile, but secondary to PERF-01/03. No number links it to a score directly; flagged as unquantified.

recommendation: Record the correction. If a payload pass happens later, the RSC payload duplication is the place to look, not images or compression, which are already fine.

title: The 281-to-242 Poor-page drop after the Marker.io removal is plausible but unverifiable from the data on disk

evidence.claim: Poor Lighthouse count fell 281 to 242 between the 6 Aug and 8 Aug Ahrefs crawls; the only production change in the window was 2fe4fcb, which removed Marker.io (148KB, 135ms blocking) from every page
evidence.source: Ahrefs dashboard reads 6 and 8 Aug; git log 2fe4fcb

evidence.claim: No per-URL Lighthouse export exists on disk to identify WHICH 39 pages moved, so the attribution cannot be tested; the 66-CSV all-issues export contains no performance report
Marker.io is confirmed absent from production HTML
evidence.source: curl 8 Aug, grep -ci marker = 0; site/src/components/third-party-scripts.tsx:138 showMarker = !(await isCanonicalSite())

impact.estimate: If confirmed, this is the first measured before-and-after of a real fix: removing 135ms of blocking moved 39 pages out of Poor, direct evidence that pages sit just under the threshold and that PERF-01 (a much larger removal) will move far more. Currently an attribution hypothesis, not a verified result; Lighthouse run-to-run variance could account for some or all of it.

recommendation: Export the per-URL Lighthouse table from the Ahrefs Site Audit UI for both crawl dates (the data exists in the dashboard, it was just not in our export) so the 39 movers can be identified and the attribution tested.
